correctness.rationale: For every odd prime \(p\) and integers \(k>b\ge1\), the proof derives the exact prime-power coefficient-fiber test from its minimal polynomial. An untouched singleton class (\(2r<p^b\)) excludes all character orders above \(p^b\). For lower orders, fewer than \(p\) positive and negative relocated terms force every coefficient difference in a cyclotomic fiber to vanish, exactly multiset congruence; matching gives the full zero set and its \(p^V-1\) count. Every depth \(0\) through \(b-1\) is attained with one move; a separate explicit \(r=p\) construction disproves extension to the threshold. Standalone CHECK.py passed 33317 exact and numerical supplementary checks. No finite enumeration is treated as an all-parameter proof.

value.rationale: Exact Fourier nulls of complete-residue cyclic sampling masks are fragile to residue-collision errors. This theorem gives a lift-independent structural explanation of precisely which notches survive (optimal p-adic matching), a sharp dimension-free fraction of original zeros that a single misregistration destroys, all attainable survival levels, and a matching law that fails exactly at a prime-sized fault pattern. These are natural exact stability and boundary invariants, not a random numeric slice. The claim is limited to its motivated sparse-collision model.
